blocks.heading: Engineered for the wheelset, built for the workshop
paragraphs: Every railway vehicle depends on its wheelsets. Their profile governs ride quality, rail wear and derailment safety; their geometry decides whether a train may run at all. HYT Engineering has concentrated on this subject since 1977, and the product range reflects it: machines that restore, build, measure and balance wheelsets, plus the depot equipment that keeps maintenance flowing.

Every machine is designed in-house in Pune and adapted to the customer's track gauge, wheel profiles and vehicle types. Where one machine is not enough, we combine several into a complete facility through our [turnkey projects](page:turnkey-project) – and support them for their working life through our [service organisation](page:services).

blocks.heading: How to choose the right wheel lathe
blocks.intro: The right machine depends less on the wheel than on your operation. Six questions narrow the choice quickly.

items.title: Does the wheelset stay in the vehicle?
items.text: To re-profile without dropping bogies, choose an underfloor lathe. If wheelsets are removed anyway during overhaul, a surface or portal lathe fits that flow.

items.title: How many wheelsets per day?
items.text: Fleet size and re-profiling interval set the workload. High-utilisation metro and EMU fleets often justify a tandem machine that handles a whole bogie in one setting.

items.title: What civil works are possible?
items.text: Underfloor lathes need a reinforced pit beneath the track. Surface and portal lathes work on removed wheelsets and need no pit under a running line – often simpler in an existing building.

items.title: Which wheel sizes and gauges?
items.text: List the smallest and largest tread diameters, axle lengths and gauges in your fleet, including vehicles you expect to buy. The machine is sized to that envelope.

items.title: Brake discs as well?
items.text: Wheel- and axle-mounted brake discs can be machined on suitable configurations. Tell us early, because it affects tooling and machine layout.

items.title: Stand-alone or part of a line?
items.text: Linked with [measuring stations](page:wheel-measuring-station) and wheelset handling, a lathe can become part of an [automated wheel shop](page:ts-wheel-shops#automation). Plan the interfaces from the start.

blocks.heading: What is the CNC Surface Wheel Lathe?
paragraphs: The CNC Surface Wheel Lathe is a high-precision machine designed for the reprofiling of railway wheelsets that have been disassembled from the rolling stock and are machined off the vehicle.

As railway wheels run on track over time, their tread profiles wear unevenly, causing vibration, noise, reduced braking efficiency and safety risks. The CNC Surface Wheel Lathe restores each wheel's profile back to the exact OEM specification in a single, automated cycle.

Wheelsets from all types of rolling stock – locomotives, coaches, wagons, metro trains and EMUs – can be machined on this lathe. A fully integrated pre- and post-machining measurement system ensures that every wheel is machined to exact tolerances, minimising material removal and extending wheel life.

items.q: What is the difference between a surface and an underfloor wheel lathe?
items.a: A surface lathe stands at floor level and machines wheelsets that have been removed from the vehicle. An [underfloor lathe](page:underfloor-wheel-lathe) works in a pit beneath the track and machines the wheelset while it stays in the vehicle.

items.q: Which model should I choose?
items.a: Start with your largest tread diameter, heaviest wheelset and daily volume. All three models take tread diameters of 750–1250 mm (depending on track gauge) and wheel widths of 75–145 mm. The YSL-08 has the shortest cycle (14–16 minutes floor to floor), the YSL-12 follows at 16–18 minutes and the single-tool-post YSL-21 at 50–60 minutes. We confirm the right model with our recommendation.

items.q: Can brake discs be machined?
items.a: Yes, on suitable configurations. The YSL-08 machines brake discs from 250 to 700 mm in diameter in the same setting as the wheels.

items.q: What foundation is needed?
items.a: A level, reinforced foundation at floor level, sized to the machine. No pit under the track is required. HYT provides the foundation drawing early in the project.

items.q: Should I choose a surface or a portal lathe?
items.a: Both machine removed wheelsets. A [portal wheel lathe](page:portal-wheel-lathe) is built around a rigid portal frame for heavy cuts in continuous wheel-shop production. A surface lathe suits depots and overhaul shops that re-profile wheelsets and brake discs alongside other overhaul work. We recommend one or the other after reviewing your workload.

blocks.heading: What is the CNC Underfloor Wheel Lathe?
paragraphs: The CNC Underfloor Wheel Lathe (Model YUL-08) is an automatic machine for the simultaneous re-profiling of new or worn wheels of railway vehicles in situ. Wheelsets of locomotives, coaches, wagons, trams and metro vehicles can be machined while still assembled in the rolling stock, and brake discs mounted on those wheelsets can be machined on the same machine.

Installed in a pit below track level, the machine lifts and centres the wheelset on four synchronised drive rollers, then reprofiles both wheels simultaneously using two CNC tool posts. Each roller is connected to a 15 kW AC motor through a heavy-duty reduction gearbox, and digital variable speed drives give infinite speed variation so the machine can cut through hard spots and skid marks.

The drive rollers float individually to compensate for wheel irregularities and maintain continuous contact, while an individual jack and hold-down device provides rigid support and clamping of the axle or bearing box. Contact-type probes measure profile and diameter before and after turning, and the CNC software uses that wear data to suggest the most economical depth of cut.

blocks.heading: What is the CNC Tandem Underfloor Wheel Lathe?
paragraphs: The CNC Tandem Underfloor Wheel Lathe (Model YUL-12T) is a pair of underfloor wheel lathes installed on a common foundation and shared infrastructure. Two vehicle-mounted wheelsets are reprofiled simultaneously in situ, without removing the wheelsets, the bogie brake gear, the axle box covers or any other component of the railway vehicle.

One machine is fixed and the second is fixed or movable, so the pair accommodates the varying wheelbases of different bogies. The standard centre distance between the two machines ranges from 1800 to 3100 mm and can be changed to suit a specific requirement.

The two CNC systems communicate with each other and exchange data, holding the difference in diameter across all four wheels of one bogie below 0.3 mm. The machines can also run under independent control, so a single wheelset can be machined when that is all that is required, and the brake discs of both wheelsets can be turned simultaneously.

items.q: How much time does a tandem lathe save?
items.a: Machining both wheelsets of a bogie in one cycle reduces reprofiling time by up to 50% compared with a single underfloor machine. Actual savings depend on your vehicles and depot routine.

items.q: How does the machine handle different bogie wheelbases?
items.a: One machine is fixed and the other traverses along the pit. It is positioned to match the wheelbase of the bogie over the pit, so vehicles with different bogies can use the same installation.

items.q: When is a portal lathe better than an underfloor lathe?
items.a: When wheelsets are removed from the vehicle as part of your maintenance process, or when defects are so deep that heavy cuts are needed. If you want to re-profile without removing wheelsets, choose an [underfloor lathe](page:underfloor-wheel-lathe).

items.q: Why does chip cross-section matter?
items.a: It describes how much material the tool can remove in one revolution. A larger cross-section means deep flats and hollow wear can be removed in fewer passes.

blocks.heading: What is the CNC Roller Type Portal Wheel Lathe?
paragraphs: The CNC Roller Type Portal Wheel Lathe (Model YPL-04) is an automatic machine in portal construction with roller drives that allow roll-through movement of wheelsets. It is suitable for the simultaneous re-profiling of new or worn wheels once the wheelset has been disassembled from the vehicle, and it also supports wheelsets with a mounted gearbox.

The wheelset is driven by six friction rollers, three per wheel, contacting the upper and lower tread flange areas. Each roller is housed in a spindle cartridge mounted on low-friction rocker arms, allowing vertical adjustment to accommodate wheel diameter variations and maintain consistent contact even on flat or oval surfaces. Controlled hydraulic pressure, regulated by a valve and nitrogen accumulator, keeps that contact stable, and the roller motors are synchronised through a master-slave control system.

Loading and unloading are fully automatic, and roll-in and roll-out from the same direction can be arranged where space is constrained. Wheelsets with an external CTRB are centred and clamped by a hydraulically actuated clamping device, and wheel- and axle-mounted brake discs can be machined as an option.

blocks.heading: What is the CNC Axle Journal Turning & Burnishing Lathe?
paragraphs: The CNC Axle Journal Turning & Burnishing Lathe (Model YTB 04) is a specialised machine for the maintenance and manufacture of railway wheelsets. It restores and finishes the axle journals – the precision bearing-seat surfaces located at each end of a railway axle.

These journal surfaces support the wheelset within the bogie bearings. Any wear, ovality, taper or surface damage can lead to premature bearing failure, excessive heat generation, increased maintenance costs and potential safety risks.

The turning operation removes worn or damaged material from the axle journal, restoring its original geometry and dimensional accuracy. CNC-controlled machining corrects ovality, taper and surface wear to bring the journal back within specification, and roller burnishing then finishes the surface to the required quality.

items.q: Why burnish after turning?
items.a: Turning leaves fine peaks on the surface. Burnishing presses them down, giving a smoother, compacted surface that supports the bearing better and resists wear and fretting.

items.q: Does burnishing remove material?
items.a: No. It is a cold-working process that displaces surface material rather than cutting it, so the diameter changes very little.

blocks.heading: Making and breaking the interference fit
paragraphs: A railway wheel is pressed on to its axle seat with a specified interference: the bore is slightly smaller than the seat. During mounting, the force rises as the wheel travels along the seat, and that force profile shows whether the joint is sound.

HYT wheel presses are built for both directions of this work. In mounting, the press positions the wheel and drives it on to the seat to the specified back-to-back distance. In dismounting, it applies the force needed to remove worn wheels from axles that will be reused.

Pressing brings together the work of other wheel-shop machines: bores from the [vertical turning and boring machine](page:vertical-turning-boring-machine), seats from the [axle turning lathe](page:axle-turning-lathe) and final checks on the [wheel measuring station](page:wheel-measuring-station).

dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.title: Dynamic Wheel Balancing Machine for Railway Wheels
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.description: HYT dynamic wheel balancing machine measures the unbalance of railway wheels and wheelsets in rotation, so it can be corrected for smoother, quieter running.
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.h1: Dynamic Wheel Balancing Machine for railway wheels and wheelsets
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.lede: An unbalanced wheel vibrates at every revolution, loading bearings and track and reducing ride comfort. The balancing machine measures how much unbalance there is and where, so it can be corrected before service.
dynamic-wheel-balancing-machine.summary: Measures the dynamic unbalance of railway wheels and wheelsets so it can be corrected before service – for smoother running and longer component life.

blocks.heading: Why balance matters as speed rises
paragraphs: Unbalance is mass that is not evenly distributed around the axis of rotation. At low speed its effect is small. The resulting force, however, grows with the square of speed, and an unbalanced wheel becomes a source of vibration for bearings, bogie, track and car body.

A dynamic balancing machine spins the wheel or wheelset and measures the forces this creates. It determines both the amount and the angular position of the unbalance, in one or two planes, so the workshop knows exactly how much material to remove or add, and where.
Operators of passenger trains, metros and multiple units commonly specify balance limits for their wheels, because ride comfort, noise and component life depend on them.

items.q: What is the difference between static and dynamic balancing?
items.a: Static balancing corrects mass distribution in a single plane. Dynamic balancing measures during rotation and can correct in two planes, which also deals with the rocking effect of unbalance across a wide wheel or a wheelset.

items.q: What balance limits apply?
items.a: Limits are set by your specification or the applicable standard for the vehicle. The machine is configured to check against them.

items.q: How is unbalance corrected?
items.a: Usually by removing material at the position shown by the machine, for example by machining; in some designs by adding mass. The method follows your wheel specification.

items.q: Can wheelsets be balanced, or only wheels?
items.a: Both are possible, depending on configuration. Tell us whether you balance single wheels, wheelsets or both.

items.q: Does a re-profiled wheel need re-balancing?
items.a: Re-profiling removes material and can change the balance. Whether re-balancing is required depends on your maintenance rules.

items.q: Which operations does the machine perform?
items.a: Commutator turning and grinding, mica undercutting, deburring and polishing, turning and grinding of bearing journals, wire and tape banding, re-rolling and coil cut-off – all on one machine.

items.q: Why undercut the mica?
items.a: Mica wears more slowly than copper. If it stands level with or above the segments, brushes ride on it, which causes uneven contact, sparking and accelerated wear.

items.q: Is the machine relevant for three-phase AC traction motors?
items.a: Three-phase AC induction motors have no commutator, so commutator work does not apply. The machine is intended for fleets with DC traction motors and other commutator machines.

items.q: Which armature sizes can be handled?
items.a: Armatures up to 30 kN, 500–1600 mm long and 130–1500 mm in diameter, with commutator diameters of 120–900 mm and commutator lengths of 75–450 mm.

blocks.heading: What is the Automated Train Washing Plant?
paragraphs: HYT's Automated Train Washing Plant removes the dependence on manual labour for coach cleaning – a critical hygiene and presentation requirement across Indian Railways depots and washing lines.

The system is designed as a fixed installation through which rakes pass at low speed. As each coach travels through the plant it is sequentially pre-wetted, chemically treated, mechanically brushed, high-pressure rinsed and mopped, all without stopping. Water recycling through an integrated effluent treatment plant (ETP) further reduces operating costs.

blocks.heading: What is the Rail Cum Road Vehicle Shunter?
paragraphs: The HYT Rail Cum Road Vehicle Shunter is a versatile rail handling solution designed to move locomotives, coaches, wagons, metro cars and complete train sets safely and efficiently within depots, workshops, maintenance facilities and production plants.

Unlike conventional shunting locomotives, the HYT Rail Cum Road Vehicle Shunter combines road mobility with rail traction capability, allowing operators to transfer rolling stock seamlessly between workshop bays, inspection lines, washing plants and storage tracks without the need for a dedicated rail locomotive.

The shunter is equipped with advanced hydraulic and traction systems, providing smooth acceleration, controlled braking and accurate positioning of rolling stock during maintenance and assembly operations. This improves operational safety, reduces turnaround time and enhances overall workshop productivity.

Designed for modern railway maintenance facilities, the HYT Rail Cum Road Vehicle Shunter offers a cost-effective and flexible alternative to traditional shunting methods, helping operators maximise asset utilisation while minimising operating costs and infrastructure requirements.

blocks.heading: Why sliding surfaces matter
paragraphs: Wherever a heavy part moves along a guide – a machine slide, a table, a carriage or a ram – the sliding surface decides how smoothly, accurately and quietly it moves, and how long it lasts. Friction, stick-slip and wear in these surfaces translate directly into lost accuracy and extra maintenance.

"Gleittechnik" is German for sliding technology, and it is SKC Gleittechnik's field. HYT Engineering is the company's exclusive distributor in India, combining the partner's products with our own experience as a builder and servicer of heavy machine tools.
Whether you are building new machines, reconditioning worn slideways or upgrading existing equipment, HYT advises on where sliding technology fits and coordinates supply with SKC.
